name: Secure Computation (MPC, FHE, ZK)
description: Secure multiparty computation, homomorphic encryption, zero-knowledge proofs, and private set operations.

uss.narrative:
The earliest USENIX Security entries here mark the moment secure computation pivoted from theory toward deployable systems. GAZELLE (USENIX 2018) showed that combining homomorphic encryption with garbled circuits could make secure neural network inference practical, while DIZK (USENIX 2018) attacked the scalability of zero-knowledge proofs by distributing SNARK generation across a cluster. Mobile Private Contact Discovery at Scale (USENIX 2019) carried the same systems-engineering spirit into private set intersection, turning a privacy-preserving primitive into something a messaging app could actually run against millions of contacts.

Around 2020-2021 the area broadened from raw primitives to real-world applications and reusable building blocks. Secure Multi-party Computation of Differentially Private Median (USENIX 2020) and Secure parallel computation on national scale volumes of data (USENIX 2020) pushed MPC toward statistics and graph workloads at scale, while DatashareNetwork (USENIX 2020) and Identifying Harmful Media in End-to-End Encrypted Communication (USENIX 2021) applied private search and membership testing to journalism and abuse detection. Poseidon (USENIX 2021) was a quiet but pivotal shift: by designing a hash function native to ZK arithmetic circuits, it became core infrastructure for the SNARK/STARK ecosystem. GForce (USENIX 2021) and Fuzzy Labeled PSI (USENIX 2021) meanwhile extended privacy-preserving inference to GPUs and biometric search.

By 2022-2023 the work matured along several distinct threads. Private set operations diversified into union, cardinality, and multi-party variants, with Linear Private Set Union (USENIX 2023) and Efficient Unbalanced PSI Cardinality (USENIX 2023) improving asymptotics and contact-tracing use cases, and Estimating Incidental Collection in Foreign Intelligence Surveillance (USENIX 2022) applying large-scale multiparty PSI to surveillance auditing. FHE became a systems-optimization target in its own right with ELASM (USENIX 2023) managing error-latency tradeoffs in CKKS-style schemes. ZK proofs moved toward concrete impact, with Cheesecloth (USENIX 2023) proving real-world vulnerabilities in zero knowledge and Eos (USENIX 2023) enabling private delegation of expensive zkSNARK provers, while GigaDORAM (USENIX 2023) broke the billion-address barrier for oblivious RAM.

The 2024 cohort shows a field that is both deeply specialized and increasingly fused with machine learning. A cluster of papers - Scalable MPC Protocols for ML in the Honest-Majority Setting, MD-ML, OblivGNN, and Scalable Zero-knowledge Proofs for Non-linear Functions in Machine Learning - target privacy-preserving and verifiable ML across threat models and architectures. FHE saw both attacks and engineering advances, with Key Recovery Attacks on Approximate Homomorphic Encryption (USENIX 2024) exposing weaknesses in noise-flooding defenses and DaCapo (USENIX 2024) automating bootstrapping management. Polynomial-commitment and secret-sharing machinery (Fast RS-IOP Multivariate Polynomial Commitments, USENIX 2024), verifiable aggregation (PINE, USENIX 2024), distributed PRFs (LaKey, USENIX 2024), and multi-party PSI (O-Ring and K-Star, USENIX 2024) round out a landscape that has moved decisively from "can we do this securely" to "how do we do it at scale, robustly, and with verified correctness."

milestones.title: Mobile Private Contact Discovery at Scale
milestones.note: scaled private set intersection to real messaging-app contact discovery, moving PSI from primitive to deployment

milestones.note: a ZK-native hash that became foundational infrastructure across the SNARK/STARK ecosystem (by far the most-cited here)

milestones.title: Cheesecloth: Zero-Knowledge Proofs of Real World Vulnerabilities
milestones.note: turned ZK proofs toward a concrete security application: demonstrating real software vulnerabilities without disclosing them

milestones.title: ELASM: Error-Latency-Aware Scale Management for Fully Homomorphic Encryption
milestones.note: treated FHE as a systems-optimization problem, managing the error-latency tradeoff in approximate (CKKS-style) computation

milestones.note: exposed practical key-recovery weaknesses in CKKS noise-flooding defenses, sharpening the security model for deployed FHE

milestones.note: representative of the 2024 convergence of MPC and machine learning at scale across threat models

top4.narrative:
The earliest works on this list show secure computation splitting into the practical tracks that still define the field. On the proof side, Bulletproofs (S&P 2018) delivered short non-interactive zero-knowledge proofs with no trusted setup, while Doubly-Efficient zkSNARKs Without Trusted Setup (S&P 2018) and DIZK (USENIX 2018) pushed toward transparent and distributable proof systems, and xJsnark (S&P 2018) made verifiable computation easier to program. In parallel, a cluster of CCS/S&P 2018 papers (Fast Multiparty Threshold ECDSA with Fast Trustless Setup, Fast Secure Multiparty ECDSA, Secure Two-party Threshold ECDSA from ECDSA Assumptions) turned MPC toward a concrete killer app: threshold signatures for cryptocurrency custody. A third thread targeted private machine learning, with GAZELLE (USENIX 2018) combining homomorphic encryption and garbled circuits for fast secure neural-network inference, and Secure Outsourced Matrix Computation (CCS 2018) doing the analogous work purely in HE.

The next phase was about making these tools usable and scalable. Compiler and systems work matured fast: HyCC (CCS 2018) and the SoK: General Purpose Compilers for Secure Multi-Party Computation (S&P 2019) organized the messy landscape of MPC toolchains, and CrypTFlow (S&P 2020) compiled real TensorFlow graphs into MPC protocols. Private ML kept growing in scope and rigor, moving from inference to training (QUOTIENT, CCS 2019; Helen, S&P 2019) and from passive to actively-secure protocols over rings (New Primitives for Actively-Secure MPC over Rings, S&P 2019). The proof line advanced toward transparent, sublinear arguments (Transparent Polynomial Delegation, S&P 2020; Ligero++, CCS 2020) and started proving statements about ML itself (Zero Knowledge Proofs for Decision Tree Predictions, CCS 2020). The threshold-ECDSA line, meanwhile, generalized to the full multiparty case (Threshold ECDSA from ECDSA Assumptions, S&P 2019) and gained proactive security and identifiable aborts (UC Non-Interactive, Proactive, Threshold ECDSA, CCS 2020), alongside asynchronous distributed key generation (CCS 2020).

By 2021 the field was optimizing hard and specializing for ZK-native infrastructure. Poseidon (USENIX 2021) gave a hash function tuned for proof systems, Wolverine (S&P 2021) scaled VOLE-based ZK to huge circuits, and SoK: Fully Homomorphic Encryption Compilers (S&P 2021) and PEGASUS (S&P 2021) made FHE more practical and expressive. Private ML hit hardware acceleration (CryptGPU, S&P 2021) and tackled hard nonlinear functions (SiRnn, S&P 2021), while Lightweight Techniques for Private Heavy Hitters (S&P 2021) showed lightweight MPC analytics at scale.

Most recently the work is application-driven and integrity-focused. Secure federated learning dominates, shifting from confidentiality alone to verifiable, robust aggregation against malicious actors (EIFFeL, CCS 2022; ELSA and RoFL, S&P 2023; Flamingo, S&P 2023). Zero-knowledge proofs moved into deployed systems: trustless cross-chain bridges (zkBridge, CCS 2022) and anonymous credentials bootstrapped from existing identity infrastructure (zk-creds, S&P 2023). And private ML has caught up to modern models, with BOLT (S&P 2024) delivering practical privacy-preserving inference for transformers — closing the loop from the simple-network inference that GAZELLE started in 2018.

milestones.title: Bulletproofs: Short Proofs for Confidential Transactions and More
milestones.note: introduced short, trustless non-interactive ZK proofs that became a workhorse for confidential transactions and range proofs

milestones.title: GAZELLE: A Low Latency Framework for Secure Neural Network Inference
milestones.note: kicked off practical secure ML inference by combining homomorphic encryption with garbled circuits for low latency

milestones.title: SoK: General Purpose Compilers for Secure Multi-Party Computation
milestones.note: systematized the fast-growing MPC compiler landscape, turning MPC from bespoke protocols into a tooling discipline

milestones.title: CrypTFlow: Secure TensorFlow Inference
milestones.note: compiled real TensorFlow models into MPC protocols, bridging mainstream ML frameworks and secure computation

milestones.title: Poseidon: A New Hash Function for Zero-Knowledge Proof Systems
milestones.note: provided a ZK-friendly hash that slashed circuit costs and became foundational infrastructure for SNARK/STARK systems

milestones.title: Wolverine: Fast, Scalable, and Communication-Efficient Zero-Knowledge Proofs for Boolean and Arithmetic Circuits
milestones.note: scaled VOLE-based zero-knowledge to billions of gates, enabling proofs over very large circuits

milestones.title: Flamingo: Multi-Round Single-Server Secure Aggregation with Applications to Private Federated Learning
milestones.note: matured single-server secure aggregation for practical multi-round private federated learning

milestones.title: BOLT: Privacy-Preserving, Accurate and Efficient Inference for Transformers
milestones.note: extended practical secure inference to modern transformer models, closing the gap with state-of-the-art ML
